topic.title: Code Models, Program Semantics, and Correctness Evaluation
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: This topic studies learning systems that generate, understand, or assess programs. It includes repository context, semantic reasoning, compiler tasks, and hardware-description representations. A representative evaluation framework creates semantically equivalent variations of programming problems to probe whether code models handle reasoning beyond familiar benchmark wording.
topic.whyItMatters: Code that appears plausible can still behave incorrectly, and public benchmarks may overlap with training data. Evaluations grounded in behavior, semantics, and controlled problem variation provide stronger evidence than surface similarity or success on a fixed test collection alone.
topic.evolution: Early representatives investigate code scheduling and structured program evolution. Later work applies language models to repository-level context and semantic training. Recent directions include dynamic contamination-aware benchmarks, selective generation based on expected correctness, and joint code–graph representations for hardware design tasks.
openQuestions: How can benchmark transformations preserve difficulty as well as semantics?
What evidence should a code model use to decide when it cannot safely produce a functionally correct answer?

papers.title: Rule2DRC: Benchmarking LLM Agents for DRC Script Synthesis with Execution-Guided Test Generation
papers.tldr: Rule2DRC evaluates chip-rule scripts through execution, while SplitTester generates distinguishing tests to improve selection among candidate programs.

papers.title: SAC-Opt: Semantic Anchors for Iterative Correction in Optimization Modeling
papers.tldr: SAC-Opt improves generated optimization models by repeatedly checking their recovered meaning against the original problem and correcting mismatches.

papers.title: Scaling Agentic Verifier for Competitive Coding
papers.tldr: Agentic Verifier learns to generate targeted tests that expose differences between candidate programs and improve solution selection.

papers.title: SemRep : Generative Code Representation Learning with Code Transformations
papers.tldr: SemRep learns semantics-preserving code transformations as an explicit representation, improving editing, optimization, and evolutionary search under matched training budgets.

papers.title: SERA: Soft-Verified Efficient Repository Agents
papers.tldr: SERA trains competitive, repository-specialized coding agents using synthetic trajectories and supervised fine-tuning at substantially reduced reported cost.

papers.title: StepCodeReasoner: Aligning Code Reasoning with Stepwise Execution Traces via Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: StepCodeReasoner trains on verifiable intermediate execution states, improving reported code reasoning, trace prediction, and generation results.

papers.title: SWE-IF: Aligning Code Evaluation with Human Preference
papers.tldr: SWE-IF evaluates code instruction following alongside correctness, producing a combined measure that better correlates with human preference.

papers.title: Towards Functional Correctness of Code Models with Selective Generation
papers.tldr: Automatically generated unit tests support selective code generation that abstains on uncertainty and theoretically controls false discoveries among accepted answers.

papers.title: UniCode: Augmenting Evaluation for Code Reasoning
papers.tldr: UniCode generates algorithmic problem variants that expose substantial performance drops and regression to memorized seed logic.

papers.title: UniRTL: Unifying Code and Graph for Robust RTL Representation Learning
papers.tldr: UniRTL aligns RTL code, functional summaries, and control data flow graphs to improve performance prediction and code retrieval.
